summary: After the break, Ustaz Azlan shares reflections from a trip to India and Sri Lanka with his father and eldest son, reading the sirah through social and economic justice. He argues that Quraysh opposed the Prophet SAW because he challenged structural injustice, not merely ritual, and links this to colonialism, structural poverty, riba and fathers separated from their families. Sirah episodes include Umm Jamil's harassment of the Prophet SAW, the covert torture of the elite, and Abu Talib's meeting with the Prophet SAW where he said 'the sun in my right hand'. He closes with a reading of Buya Hamka's address to the Prophet SAW on the independence of Malaya.
keyPoints: Quraysh left the Prophet SAW alone for 40 years and opposed him only when he challenged injustice and the system that served the elite.
The sirah is not only about ritual; the early Makkan verses stress orphans, the poor, baby girls and social justice.
Colonialism looted a subcontinent that once held about 25% of the world economy and left ethnic divisions.
Riba is the only sin Allah declared war over because it kills many lives systemically.
Umm Jamil harassed the Prophet SAW full-time and called him 'Mudhammam'; Allah turned her sight away from him.
Abu Talib nearly wavered but was strengthened by the Prophet's SAW reply that he would not stop even if given the sun and moon.
Learning history, starting with family history, gives purpose and gratitude.

lessons.title: Study the sirah while travelling
lessons.body: Travel opens the eyes to the sirah and the state of the ummah.

lessons.title: Critique the system, not only ritual
lessons.body: Quraysh tolerated the Prophet SAW for 40 years and opposed him only when he challenged injustice.

lessons.title: Longing for the Prophet SAW needs action
lessons.body: The companions did not stay weeping at his grave but spread across the world.

lessons.title: Two percent who stand firm is enough
lessons.body: Change can happen with about two percent willing to sacrifice.

lessons.title: Freedom of mind and identity
lessons.body: Be proud of our own language, food and culture; do not judge ourselves by the coloniser.

lessons.title: Reject racism and demonisation
lessons.body: Championing one's ethnicity is fine but looking down on others and stirring enmity is jahiliyyah.

lessons.title: Care about structural poverty
lessons.body: Foreign labourers separated from their families result from colonialism and poverty; show empathy.

lessons.title: Riba impoverishes systemically
lessons.body: Unlike zakat, which closes the gap, riba widens it between rich and poor.

lessons.title: Help first while fighting the structure
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW fed people while challenging structures; do not wait for the structure to be fixed before helping.

lessons.title: A partner who absorbs pressure
lessons.body: Khadijah strengthened the Prophet SAW daily after pressure outside.

lessons.title: Appreciate the hardship of earlier people
lessons.body: Studying family and national history brings appreciation and gratitude.

lessons.title: Sirah is a subject to repeat
lessons.body: Tariq Suwaidan taught sirah seven times; we have barely scratched the surface.

dalil.context: The command to declare war from Allah and His Messenger on those who persist in riba. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: If you do not, then be warned of war from God and His Messenger. You shall have your capital if you repent, and without suffering loss or causing others to suffer loss.

dalil.context: The riba-eater rises like one possessed by Satan. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: But those who take usury will rise up on the Day of Resurrection like someone tormented by Satan’s touch. That is because they say, ‘Trade and usury are the same,’ but God has allowed trade and forbidden usury. Whoever, on receiving God’s warning, stops taking usury may keep his past gains- God will be his judge- but whoever goes back to usury will be an inhabitant of the Fire, there to remain.

dalil.context: Ibn Abbas explains the meaning of war on Allah.
dalil.translation: On the Day of Resurrection the riba-eater will be given weapons to fight Allah and His Messenger.

dalil.context: Surah Al-Ma'un describes the denier of the faith who neglects orphans and the poor. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: [Prophet], have you considered the person who denies the Judgement?

dalil.context: Wealth must not circulate only among the rich. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: Whatever gains God has turned over to His Messenger from the inhabitants of the villages belong to God, the Messenger, kinsfolk, orphans, the needy, the traveller in need- this is so that they do not just circulate among those of you who are rich––so accept whatever the Messenger gives you, and abstain from whatever he forbids you. Be mindful of God: God is severe in punishment.

dalil.context: In Sahih Bukhari; the Prophet SAW said Quraysh were insulting 'Mudhammam' while he is Muhammad.
dalil.translation: Umm Jamil came with a stone looking for 'Mudhammam', and Allah turned her sight away from the Prophet SAW sitting beside Abu Bakr.

dalil.context: A famous sirah report from Ibn Hisham and Dala'il an-Nubuwwah.
dalil.translation: By Allah, uncle, if they placed the sun in my right hand and the moon in my left to make me abandon this matter, I would not leave it until Allah makes it prevail or I perish for it.

dalil.context: Abu Talib recalled the Prophet SAW, who had wept and left.
dalil.translation: Go and do as you please; by Allah I will never hand you over.

sirah.summary: Quraysh stepped up pressure on the Prophet SAW and on his protector Abu Talib.
